urgency: normal — mobile-dev cannot be briefed until this and 20260803-ff-003 both land.
objective: Produce the complete token set for Direction B, dark-only, anchored on brand gold #C4A24A, with every token named and valued and every pair the design actually uses measured for contrast.
success_criteria: Every token is named and given a concrete value — hex, px, ms, or numeric weight. No adjectives standing in for values, nothing left as 'as proposed'.
The gold ramp is derived from #C4A24A and each step is measured individually against all four surfaces; no step inherits another's ratio.
The functional blue is named with a concrete hex and measured against all four surfaces.
Contrast is given for every foreground token against every one of the four surfaces, with each result labelled AAA / AA / AA-large / FAIL, and every FAIL carrying a stated usage restriction.
The warning-hue collision is resolved with an explicit choice and its cost stated — not merely acknowledged.
The gold-derived replacements for the voided primary, accent, glow and gradient tokens are specified and measured.
The font specification names each family, its weights, and whether it is declared locally or fetched, with a recommendation and reason.
The spec states it is dark-only and names the main.dart change that dark-only requires.

context.label: Brand anchor and the correction that produced it
context.body:
FaithFeed's brand is GOLD. An earlier brief in this sequence stated the brand was
blue (#1d5fa7 / #64aeed); that was wrong — those hexes came from stale assets and stale
docs, not from the operator. Any colour reasoning anchored on blue is void.

BRAND GOLD #C4A24A — operator-confirmed, single flat value, from the Alpha-and-Omega
monogram. Measured (WCAG 2.x, sRGB):
    hue 43.3 deg, relative luminance 0.3807
    on #0B0E14  7.92 AAA    on #12161F  7.42 AAA
    on #1A2030  6.66 AA     on #232B40  5.78 AA
    on #FFFFFF  2.44 FAIL   on #F5F3EF  2.20 FAIL
Gold is a dark-surface colour. Never specify it as text, or as a meaningful graphical
object, on a light surface. Any lighter or darker gold you derive must be measured
individually — ramp steps do not inherit these ratios.

context.label: The chosen direction, what carries forward, and what is void
context.body:
DIRECTION B — HALO GLASS, MADE DARK-ONLY. This is the operator's choice.

Dark-only is deliberate, not a scope cut: gold fails on every light surface measured
above, so a light companion would need a different anchor and would be a different
direction. Specify B as dark-only and say so explicitly.

CARRIED FORWARD — neutrals, chosen as neutrals rather than derived from any brand anchor,
so they survive the blue-to-gold correction. Re-measure anything you reuse:
  canvas #0B0E14 | surface #12161F | surface-elevated #1A2030 | surface-highlight #232B40
  on-surface #F4F6FB -> 17.87 / 16.74 / 15.01 / 13.02, all AAA
  on-surface-variant #A9B2C6 -> 9.09 / 8.52 / 7.64 AAA, 6.62 AA
  on-surface-muted #6E7893 -> 4.40 / 4.12 / 3.69 FAIL normal, 3.21 AA-large only
  success #34D399 all AAA | error #F87171 all AA | warning #FBBF24 all AAA

VOID — blue-derived, must be re-specified around gold:
  primary #64aeed, primary-strong #1d5fa7, accent-violet #7C5CFC,
  'Halo Primary' #1D5FA7->#64AEED->#7C5CFC, 'Aurora' #00C9FF->#64AEED->#7C5CFC.
  'Ember' #FB7185->#FBBF24 is not blue-derived — keep or retire on its own merits.

CARRIED FORWARD — non-colour groups, palette-independent:
  Type: Sora via google_fonts, weights 400/500/600/700, replacing Urbanist in both
    ThemeData.apply() calls and every ad hoc fontFamily:'Urbanist' site including the
    main.dart wordmark. No serif, no monospace.
  Elevation: shadow is near-invisible on near-black, so depth reads as layered surface
    colour plus a coloured glow. e1: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.6) + 1px border rgba(255,255,255,.06);
    e2: 0 8px 24px <glow> + 1px border rgba(255,255,255,.08);
    e3: 0 16px 40px <glow> + 1px border rgba(255,255,255,.10).
    The glow colours were blue and violet — VOID. Re-specify against gold and measure.
  Radius: xs 6 / sm 10 / md 16 / lg 24 / full 999.
  Spacing (4px grid): 4/8/12/16/20/28/40. Touch target min 48px.
  Motion: instant 80 / fast 150 / standard 220 / slow 320 ms; easing-standard
    cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1); one signature spring (mass 1, stiffness 280, damping 22)
    reserved for the floating AI button and AI-surface entrances only.
  Glass: B's identity. glass-fill = surface-elevated at 55% alpha over blurred content,
    blur sigma 20; glass-border = on-surface at 12% alpha, 1px. Scoped to CHROME ONLY —
    modals, bottom sheets, nav bar, floating AI button — explicitly NOT list or feed
    cards, because per-card blur inside a scrolling ListView is the real performance
    cost behind the 16 measured BackdropFilter sites.

PALETTE POLICY — GOLD BRAND OVER BLUE FUNCTIONAL.
  Gold #C4A24A is the brand and premium accent: brand moments, primary CTAs, premium
  badges, selected brand states. Keep it scarce and deliberate.
  Blue is RETAINED as the functional interactive hue — links, selection, focus rings,
  active states, informational chrome. This is partly a cost argument the spec must
  respect: AppTheme.primaryTeal alone is 930 call sites already resolving to a blue, and
  most are functional UI rather than brand expression. Keeping them functional-blue makes
  most of that migration a rename instead of a thousand-site re-colour. Gold and blue sit
  164.3 deg apart, near-complementary, so this is a real pairing. Name the functional blue
  explicitly and measure it against all four surfaces; it need not remain #64aeed.

A COLLISION TO RESOLVE, NOT NOTE.
  Brand gold is hue 43.3. warningAmber #F59E0B is 37.7 — 5.6 deg away, the same hue
  family. highlightYellow #F5EB30 is 13.7 deg away, also colliding. A user cannot read
  gold as brand/premium and amber as warning when they are the same hue. Either move the
  warning hue or restrict gold so the two never share a surface. State which, and its cost.
  holyGold is defined at app_theme.dart:77 as an alias of highlightYellow, so it is not
  gold and inherits this collision.

context.label: Where to read the current visual system
context.body:
You are running with the FaithFeed repository as your working directory. Read
lib/theme/app_theme.dart and pubspec.yaml directly rather than trusting any summary of
them. If a path is missing, return status "blocked" and name it rather than substituting
a similar file.

context.label: Measured survey — counts, fonts, and theme constants

constraints:
Tokens and rationale only — no code, no diffs, no edits. You have no write tool.

Do NOT produce the legacy-constant mapping, the per-call-site application rules, or the migration order. Those are 20260803-ff-003 and doing them here is what made the previous version of this brief exceed its time budget. Stop at the token set.

The font fix is in scope and non-negotiable. A family the build cannot load renders as a silent fallback, so a token set specified against an unloadable family is the current bug with new names.

Specify against what the repository actually contains, not what the survey says, where the two disagree — and say so when they do.

Gate rationale: this task touches no approval gate. It produces a specification; nothing is published, promoted, or spent, and no code changes.
out_of_scope: The legacy-constant mapping, application rules for unmapped call sites, and the migration order — all 20260803-ff-003. Writing or editing application code. Deciding flows, screen structure, or component behaviour — that is ui-ux. Redesigning the logo or brand mark. Reopening the direction choice or the gold anchor; both are operator decisions already made.
expected_deliverables: The complete Direction B dark-only token set, every token named and valued
The gold ramp derived from #C4A24A, each step measured
The functional blue, named and measured
Contrast table: every foreground token against all four surfaces, with restrictions on every failing pair
The warning-hue collision resolution, with its cost
Gold-derived replacements for the voided primary, accent, glow and gradient tokens
The font specification, with a local-vs-fetch recommendation
The main.dart dependency that dark-only requires
